Job Summary

The Ops Project Manager II leads and supports assigned projects and initiatives of medium to high complexity applying project management methodology to support the company and group’s strategy. Manage assigned projects through the various stages of the project lifecycle, from concept to launching. This includes developing SOW, business proposals, functional requirements, project plan w/milestones and implementation plan. Provide management and guidance toward successful collaboration with multi-functional groups and direct project team responsible for implementation of Jabil’s strategies.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Define concise goals and objectives within a project framework
Ensure all project requirements and/or objectives are correctly gathered, understood and properly translated for execution
Define and recognize project Key Performance Indicators and manage the work within scope, quality, time and cost constraints
Conduct project risk reviews and appropriate mitigation
Facilitate communication as appropriate to all involved and "manage" the stakeholders This includes escalate issues to the next level of management
Collaborates in determining forecast project budget and staffing needs for current and future site needs
Accountable for overall project success - including cost, schedule, quality, and scope management
Accountable for customer satisfaction both internal and external to project success

Understand and exceed customer (internal or external) needs and expectations
Identify creative ways to implement corrective actions in cost effective manner
Utilize tools to track changes and identify cost impact for review with senior management
Provide feedback to project team and leaders on concerns with cost
Drive the wider team to continuously improve in key operational metrics and the achievement of the project & organizational goals

Provide regular project updates to project team, relevant departments, stakeholders, project champions and senior leadership as needed
Works with stakeholders to define project road maps and deliverables

Establish and maintain communications with both customer personnel and senior management as needed

Builds and structures integrated teams to ensure maximum performance; provides direction and motivation
Could provide mentorship and coaching to project team members Gives and receives both written and verbal feedback
Identify and prepare proposals that close gaps and mitigate risk
Adhere to all safety and health rules and regulations associated with this position and as directed by supervisor
Comply and follow all procedures within the company security policy
May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned

KNOWLEDGE REQUIREMENTS

Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously
Ability to form and lead strong multi-functional teams to achieve company and customer (internal or external) objectives
Organize verbal and written ideas clearly and use an appropriate business style
Ability to effectively present information to management and/or customer personnel
Ability to respond in a timely fashion to common inquiries or complaints
Define, develop and implement strategies contribute to the overall company and group strategic direction
Demonstrate high performance orientation, detail orientation, market knowledge and sound judgment
Demonstrate ability to build and leverage partnerships, implement change and manage projects
Proficiency in use of personal computers, Microsoft Office products (Excel, Word and PowerPoint) and e-mail skills required
Advanced PC skills, including training and knowledge of Jabil’s software packages in an integrated system such as SAP

Bachelor’s degree required
Minimum of 5+ years of experience
Desired experience in Management/ supervisory role
Minimum of 1-year experience leading projects or in project management
PMP Certification or equivalent preferred
Or an equivalent combination of education, experience and / or training

jobs.title: Time & Attendance Project Manager
jobs.description:
Project Manager - Time & Attendance (T&A) Brazil

Division: Weir Minerals

Location: Brazil (remote)

What We Do At Weir

We are a global leader in mining technology for a sustainable future. We help our customers extract the resources the world needs more efficiently and more sustainably. Our planet’s future depends on the transition to renewable energy, and that transition can only happen with the metals and minerals our customers deliver. So, we work side by side with mines across the globe to move less rock, use less energy, use water wisely, and create less waste. Together, we drive the shift to smart, efficient, and more sustainable mining.

Make your impact

As the T&A Project Manager for Brazil,
you will lead the successful delivery of Time & Attendance solutions across Brazil, driving implementation activities and execution throughout the project lifecycle.

This is a hands-on delivery leadership role,
combining project governance with active involvement in day-to-day project execution. Acting as the primary coordination point between business stakeholders, implementation partners, and global program leadership, you will manage vendor delivery, stakeholder engagement, and business readiness activities to ensure successful, compliant, and sustainable T&A implementations

What You’ll Do

Project Planning & Governance: Develop and maintain project plans, milestones, dependencies, resource requirements, governance frameworks, and documentation, ensuring alignment with global program objectives, regional business needs, and implementation partner methodologies.
Project Delivery & Vendor Management: Lead end-to-end T&A implementations across North America, coordinating cross-functional teams, implementation partners, and technology vendors to deliver all project phases, from requirements gathering and solution design through testing, go-live, and transition to ongoing support.
Risk, RAIDD & Readiness Management: Manage RAIDD governance, proactively identifying risks, issues, actions, decisions, and dependencies, while overseeing mitigation plans, stage-gate readiness assessments, operational preparedness, and go-live approvals across multiple countries and business units.
Change Management & Adoption: Partner with change, communications, and training teams to drive business readiness, user adoption, process standardization, and successful implementation of future-state workforce management processes, balancing global standards with regional operational and compliance requirements.
Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement: Provide project reporting and executive communications, including status updates, milestone tracking, project health indicators, resource and budget impacts, governance materials, and escalation of critical issues, while building strong relationships with business and leadership stakeholders.
Safety First: Demonstrate 100% commitment to our zero harm behaviors in support of our drive towards developing a world-class safety culture.

What You’ll Bring

Must-haves:

2 - 5 years leading Time & Attendance (T&A), Workforce Management (WFM), or Timekeeping system implementations
Experience delivering end-to-end projects across multiple countries, including vendor and implementation partner management.
Knowledge of Brazilian payroll processes, labor legislation, tax requirements, compliance obligations, and integrations between Payroll, T&A, HRIS, and Finance systems.
Proficiency with workforce management platforms such as GeoVictoria, Ahgora,ADP eTime, ADP Essential, ADP EZ Labour, UKG, WorkForce Software, Dayforce, SAP SuccessFactors Time, Workday Time Tracking, or similar solutions.
Strong understanding of T&A processes, Payroll/HRIS integrations, RAIDD governance, project reporting, and executive stakeholder communication.
Fluent in Portuguese and English (written and spoken).

Nice-to-haves:

Project Management Professional (PMP), PRINCE2 Practitioner, Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM), or equivalent project management certification
Agile, Scrum, or other project delivery certifications
Experience supporting payroll service delivery models, including exposure to Brazilian collective bargaining agreements and workforce management practices.
Familiarity with SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central, Workday, Oracle HCM, or similar HR technology platforms.
Experience working in global transformation initiatives within complex, matrixed organizations.
Spanish is a plus.

Why join Weir?

We live our values we think safety first, do the right thing, respect each other, aim high, and delight our customers. We encourage our people to lead by example and celebrate our successes.

We’re passionate about our purpose to help deliver the natural resources that are essential to create a better future for the world. We do this by combining our deep customer insights, world-class engineering, materials science expertise, and intelligent automation to deliver innovative end-to-end solutions incorporating our signature technologies.

We believe your voice matters and your ideas make a difference. We’re working hard to nurture a diverse culture where our people feel like they belong and can do the best work of their lives. You can help shape our unique culture through our inclusion networks and safety initiatives.

Benefits

Competitive pay
Access to global inclusion networks
Regional and team-specific benefits
Sharebuilder scheme
Wellness support for you and your family
Collaboration with global teams

jobs.title: Project Manager II - Radiology
jobs.description:
Company Description

At Intelerad, we believe the path to answers in healthcare should be clear-whether you are waiting for a diagnosis or trying to expedite one. Our medical imaging solutions streamline the flow of information, simplifying complex processes, maximizing efficiencies, and shining a light on the unknown. We empower physicians to get patients the answers they need faster and improve outcomes for everyone. With more accessible imaging, we are getting patients out of the dark.

Headquartered in Raleigh, NC and Montreal, Intelerad has nearly 800 employees located in offices across four countries. The company empowers nearly 2,000 healthcare organizations around the world with the speed, scalability, and simplicity needed to increase business performance while, most importantly, improving patient outcomes. Intelerad’s modern enterprise solutions have been acknowledged by a Best in KLAS recognition, ranking #1 for PACS Asia/Oceania in the 2021 Best in KLAS: Global Software (Non-US) report.

Job Description

The Project Manager II leads successful delivery of medium to large-scale Radiology and Cardiology Healthcare IT solutions. This role coordinates Professional Services resources, manages complex project schedules, and ensures customer satisfaction through proactive communication and issue resolution while delivering projects within tight timelines and budget constraints, mentoring junior team members, and driving cross-functional collaboration to achieve optimal client outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Lead project delivery by planning, executing, and delivering medium to large-sized Radiology and Cardiology Healthcare IT implementation projects, ensuring on-time and on-budget completion while maintaining high quality standards and realizing full value of software and services through all stages of implementation from initial planning through successful go-live and beyond.
Manage customer relationships by serving as primary point of contact for assigned customer projects, building trusted advisor relationships through proactive communication, developing deep understanding of client environments, and consistently delivering project milestones to ensure customer satisfaction.
Coordinate cross-functional resources by facilitating Professional Services team collaboration, managing escalations across departments to resolve complex customer issues, and ensuring seamless project execution while monitoring project budgets, tracking resource utilization, and implementing cost-effective solutions to deliver projects within approved financial parameters.
Mentor Project Manager I team members by providing guidance on best practices and contributing to professional development of junior staff through knowledge sharing and collaborative problem-solving.

Qualifications

Qualifications & Experience

3+ years of experience in Project Management roles, preferably in healthcare technology or software implementation
Bachelor's degree in Project Management, Business Administration, or related field, or equivalent experience
Strong understanding of project management methodologies and best practices
Demonstrated experience managing medium to large-scale technology implementations
Excellent communication, negotiation, and leadership capabilities
Proven ability to build relationships with clients at operational and executive levels
Experience coordinating cross-functional teams and managing multiple concurrent projects
Flexibility to accommodate client schedules across different time zones

Preferred Qualifications & Special Requirements

PMP certification or ability to achieve certification within 12 months of hire
PRINCE 2 certification
Experience with healthcare IT solutions, particularly Radiology and/or Cardiology systems
Previous experience in Professional Services or client-facing implementation roles
Demonstrated track record of successful project delivery in international or remote team environments
Availability for occasional after-hours communication to support critical project milestones

Travel Requirements

Willingness to travel up to 20%

jobs.title: Renovation Project Manager
jobs.description:
Hiring 3 Project Managers

Locations: North Central Indiana, South Central Indiana, and Indianapolis area

American Senior Communities Renovation Project Manager

American Senior Communities is seeking a skilled Renovation Project Manager
to lead capital improvement, renovation, remodeling, and facility upgrade projects across our senior living and healthcare portfolio. This is an exciting opportunity for a construction professional who enjoys managing projects from concept through completion while making a meaningful difference in the environments where residents live and employees work.

This flexible, remote position offers the opportunity to manage projects across multiple locations while partnering with facility leadership, operations teams, contractors, and executive leadership to deliver high-quality results.

What You'll Do

As our Renovation Project Manager, you will oversee the complete lifecycle of renovation and capital improvement projects, ensuring quality, safety, budget, schedule, and operational continuity.

Project Planning

Manage assigned annual capital improvement and renovation projects from initial planning through completion.
Collaborate with facility leadership and operations teams to identify, prioritize, and scope improvement opportunities.
Develop project scopes, budgets, schedules, bid packages, and construction documentation.
Coordinate architects, engineers, consultants, contractors, and specialty vendors.
Evaluate existing conditions, identify project risks, and recommend cost-effective solutions.

Pre-Construction

Manage assigned annual capital improvement and facility renovation programs.
Collaborate with facility leadership, operations personnel, maintenance teams, and executive leadership to identify, prioritize, and scope renovation projects.
Develop detailed scopes of work, construction documents, bid packages, and project budgets.
Establish project schedules that align with operational requirements and capital funding schedules.
Review existing conditions and conduct site investigations to identify potential risks, constructability concerns, and budget impacts.
Coordinate consultants including architects, engineers, surveyors, specialty consultants, and testing agencies as required.
Develop value engineering recommendations to maximize project value without compromising quality or resident experience.
Maintain complete project documentation within company project management systems.

Construction & Project Management

Lead renovation projects through bidding, construction, and final completion.
Conduct regular site visits to monitor progress, quality, safety, and contractor performance.
Coordinate construction activities with facility operations to minimize disruption to residents, staff, and visitors.
Manage project schedules, meetings, submittals, change orders, and construction documentation.
Resolve project challenges and maintain accountability for contractor performance.

Budget & Financial Oversight

Develop and manage project budgets and cost forecasts.
Review contractor payment applications and verify work completed.
Monitor project expenditures, change orders, and contingency budgets.
Identify value engineering and cost-saving opportunities.
Provide regular project updates and financial reporting to leadership.

Safety, Quality & Compliance

Promote safe construction practices and ensure contractor compliance with OSHA and company standards.
Maintain appropriate resident protections, infection control measures, and life safety requirements during construction.
Ensure projects meet applicable building codes, healthcare regulations, and quality standards.
Protect the integrity of occupied healthcare and senior living environments throughout construction.

Project Closeout & Post-Construction

Coordinate punch lists, inspections, final documentation, and project closeout.
Ensure completion of warranties, as-built drawings, and operation and maintenance manuals.
Support annual capital planning, cost forecasting, and facility improvement prioritization.
Evaluate project performance and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

What You'll Need

Bachelor’s Degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Business, or a related field preferred.
At least 5 years of construction project management experience.
Experience managing renovation, remodeling, or capital improvement projects.
Experience in healthcare, senior living, hospitality, multifamily, commercial, or other occupied facilities preferred.
Strong knowledge of construction methods, budgeting, scheduling, procurement, and contract administration.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and contracts.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Microsoft Project, Procore, Con-Scan, or similar construction management software preferred.
Strong communication, organizational, negotiation, and leadership skills.
Ability to travel regularly to project locations for day trips.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation will be competitive and commensurate with the candidate’s experience, qualifications, leadership ability, and the value they bring to the role.

Jackson’s Realty & Builders offers a benefits package that includes (but not limited to):

Health insurance benefits
401(k) retirement plan
Paid time off (PTO)
Performance-based bonus opportunity
Continuing education
Opportunity for long-term growth within a stable, family-owned development and construction organization

Why Join Turtle Creek Management and Jackson’s Realty & Builders?

Build projects that directly improve the lives of seniors, families, and care providers.
Work for a respected, family-owned organization with more than six decades of success.
Join a stable company that develops, owns, and builds many of its own facilities.
Take ownership of projects from the ground up and see your leadership make a visible difference.
Work alongside experienced development, construction, and operations professionals.
Be part of a team that values integrity, craftsmanship, accountability, teamwork, and long-term relationships.

Our energy and logistics division serves as a top supplier of fuel, employing one of the largest tanker fleets and providing critical services to oil operations in our nation's busiest basins. Pilot Company supports a growing portfolio of brands with expertise in supply chain and retail operations, logistics and transportation, technology and digital innovation, construction, maintenance, human resources, finance, sales and marketing.

Founded in 1958 by Jim A. Haslam II and currently led by CEO Adam Wright, our founding values, people-first culture and commitment to giving back remains true to us today. DMI, LLC is seeking an IT Project Manager

The successful candidate will lead the planning, execution, and delivery of strategic IT initiatives supporting mission-critical applications, enterprise systems, and infrastructure services within a federal environment. Duties And Responsibilities

Project Leadership & Delivery

Application Transition & Modernization

Lead discovery efforts, application assessments, and transition readiness reviews.
Develop transition plans, knowledge transfer strategies, transition schedules, and operational runbooks.
Coordinate data migration, environment validation, testing, and production cutover activities.
Ensure continuity of operations and minimize disruption during transition events.
Track and report application transition milestones, risks, and dependencies.

Contract Transition Management
Support contract phase-in and transition activities for newly awarded federal programs and task orders.
Develop and execute contract transition plans in collaboration with government customers and corporate leadership.
Manage staffing transitions, onboarding activities, knowledge transfer sessions, and operational handoffs.
Coordinate transition activities with incumbent contractors, subcontractors, and agency stakeholders.
Identify and mitigate transition-related risks to ensure uninterrupted service delivery.
Establish and monitor transition success criteria and performance measures.

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement
Serve as a trusted advisor and primary point of contact for government program managers and technical leadership.
Prepare and deliver project status reports, executive summaries, and performance dashboards.
Build productive relationships with client stakeholders and internal leadership teams.
Support governance processes, change control boards, and program management reviews.

Risk, Compliance & Quality Management
Identify, document, and mitigate project risks, issues, and dependencies.
Ensure compliance with federal security, privacy, and operational requirements.
Support audits, contract deliverables, quality assurance reviews, and corrective action initiatives.
Maintain project documentation in accordance with PMO, agency, and contractual standards.

Qualifications

Education and Years of Experience:

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration, or related discipline. Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
Minimum of 3 years of IT project management experience.
Minimum of 5 years supporting federal government IT programs or contracts.
Demonstrated experience supporting application transition, migration, modernization, or onboarding efforts.
Experience managing project schedules, budgets, resources, and subcontractor performance.
Strong understanding of SDLC methodologies, Agile practices, and IT service management principles.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with experience briefing senior government officials and executives.

Required Skills

Federal Project Management
Stakeholder Relationship Management
Risk and Issue Resolution
Resource and Financial Management
Strategic Planning and Execution
Process Improvement and Operational Excellence
Team Leadership and Mentorship

Preferred Skills

Prior experience supporting the SEC or other federal civilian agencies.
Experience working in regulated or financial industry environments.
Experience with cloud migration, DevSecOps, application modernization, and enterprise transformation initiatives.
Experience managing geographically dispersed technical teams.
Familiarity with Microsoft Project, Azure DevOps, Jira, ServiceNow, Confluence, and Microsoft 365 collaboration tools.

Project Management Professional (PMP)

Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. Our unified platform bridges the gap between AI capabilities and human creativity, and lets professional creatives and designers harness the power of the world’s leading AI models without losing precision, expression, or soul. Together, we’re building tools that help people move faster without sacrificing quality, precision, or craft - a platform where AI supports creativity instead of flattening it.

We’re looking for a scrappy, hands-on AI Product Technical Program Manager to join Figma Weave as the team’s first TPM. You’ll partner with Engineering, Product, and Design to turn ambiguous customer needs and new AI capabilities into reliable creative workflows. You’ll lead programs across the AI model lifecycle, usage economics, and products like the Weave API. You’ll get close to the architecture, help teams make informed technical tradeoffs, and stay accountable through launch and adoption. You’ll also build AI workflows and automation yourself to help the team move faster.

This full-time role can be based in our New York hub or remotely on the East Coast of the United States. You’ll join a team spread across the United States, Europe, and Tel Aviv, with occasional travel to work alongside Figma Weave partners in Tel Aviv.

What you’ll do at Figma Weave:

Lead model lifecycle management across image, video, editing, enhancement, audio/lip-sync, 3D, and vector models, using the existing evaluation process to drive new model integration, launch, updates, and deprecation
Make tradeoffs around quality, reliability, latency, cost, and capacity clear to the decision owners
Track model limitations, integration issues, and provider dependencies through fixes, rollout, and follow-up
Work with Engineering, Partnerships, and Finance on provider agreements, quotas, rate limits, and capacity commitments so Weave can support product growth and launch demand. Bring in Product, Legal, and Security to resolve dependencies
Manage AI costs, capacity, and unit economics across 10+ providers and 50+ models. Forecast usage and spend, plan provider capacity for launches, and work with engineers on fallback options
Build things that make work less work. Improve process design and build AI workflows and automation that help the team move faster. Use APIs, scripts, or data queries to improve program visibility, streamline processes, and remove recurring bottlenecks
Lead horizontal product programs that span Weave teams, such as the Weave API. Understand how API contracts, authentication, permissions, asynchronous execution, and usage limits affect delivery. Coordinate dependencies across Weave and Figma, work through technical blockers, and follow the program through testing, release, and adoption
Lead cross-functional technical readiness for Config and other major launches. Work with engineering leads on end-to-end workflow testing, provider capacity, monitoring, and rollback plans. Bring together Support, Legal, Marketing, and other launch partners, make risks and go/no-go decisions clear, and follow through on customer issues and incident action items after release

We’d love to hear from you if you have:

Scrappiness and adaptability: You get into the details and take practical steps to move work forward. You can investigate a problem, partner with your engineering counterparts on a solution, or build a quick prototype without waiting for a perfect plan. You adjust when priorities change and follow through on what you start
Third-party AI model integration: You’ve led programs that bring third-party AI models into a product and keep them working. You can use evaluation findings and usage data to drive decisions across Engineering, Product, and Partnerships, including tradeoffs around quality, reliability, latency, cost, capacity, and unit economics
AI-enabled process design and automation: Hands-on experience building lightweight processes by leveraging AI workflows, automation, or internal tools
Technical judgment and hands-on problem solving: You can follow a workflow from the user interface through backend services and external model APIs. You reason about latency, throughput, rate limits, retries, and failure modes with engineers. You’ve managed AI cost structures, including usage and spend, pricing negotiations, and capacity planning
AI product program delivery and ownership: You’ve led customer-facing technical programs with cross-functional partners, from an ambiguous need through launch and adoption. You judge success by whether the product works for customers and delivers the intended result

While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

You’ve been an early TPM or worked at a startup, where you helped engineering teams plan and ship without adding more process than they needed
You’ve worked with a broad set of model providers, including early-access programs or model migrations
AI research or applied AI program experience is preferred. You’ve partnered with researchers and engineers and used their findings to bring new capabilities into a product. Experience with generative image or video products, and how creative users judge output quality, is especially useful

jobs.title: Order Resolution Program Manager
jobs.description:
Positition

The Order Resolution Program Manager builds and leads the Order Resolution Program (ORP), a national program that helps ensure patients receive the testing their physicians have ordered. When an order encounters a barrier, such as an unreachable patient, an incorrect phone number, a patient with unanswered questions about their test, or a step that requires clinic involvement, this role makes sure the right people take the right action so care is not delayed. Many of these patients are navigating a cancer diagnosis, and the program exists to support them and the Patient Coordinators who care for them.

As the program's founding owner , the Program Manager exercises independent judgment to assess the current landscape, resolve complex cases directly, and determine what the program needs to succeed, including whether and how to expand the team. The role is hands-on by design: the Program Manager works open cases alongside Patient Coordinators to understand where and why orders stall, then uses that firsthand insight and program data to set strategy, define standards, and guide leadership decisions.

The Program Manager partners across Patient Services, Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Patient Coordinators, Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers, earning alignment through expertise and sound judgment rather than direct authority.

Primary Responsibilities

Program Strategy & Ownership

Own the Order Resolution Program end-to-end across all national regions, independently assessing the current landscape, including case volume, root causes, regional variation, and existing workflows, to determine where patient orders are most at risk of delay.
Develop a data-supported program roadmap and staffing recommendation for Patient Services leadership, including headcount requirements, staffing structure, timeline, and whether process or tooling solutions would better serve patients.
Define the program operating model, including case ownership, escalation criteria, service timelines, handoff protocols, and quality standards, and adjust it as the program matures.
Lead the design of the team structure, role definitions, hiring profile, onboarding, and performance expectations for future team members.

Case Resolution & Patient Care Support

Exercise independent judgment to evaluate open ORP cases, determine the root cause of each barrier, and develop a tailored resolution strategy that accounts for the clinical context, the patient's circumstances, and available resources.
Work complex and high-priority cases directly, including researching LIMS, paper orders, and patient outreach tools to locate missing or updated contact information, and decide whether a case calls for administrative resolution, clinic education or engagement, or escalation.
Partner with Patient Coordinators to support patient outreach, providing guidance on how to approach each case and, where appropriate, connecting with patients directly so that questions about their orders are answered and care can move forward.
Determine when to escalate a case to the clinic, engage the field team, or close it, and document the rationale so any subsequent owner can continue seamlessly.
Maintain a real-time view of all open cases, including status, owner, next action, and age, and follow up consistently to confirm actions are completed and patients are not left waiting.

Analytics & Performance Reporting

Design, build, and maintain the ORP reporting infrastructure, including dashboards, KPI scorecards, and regional trend analysis, and define the metrics used to measure program success.
Report regularly to Patient Services leadership on case volume, resolution rates, time to resolution, and order completion outcomes, translating data into clear insights about what is working, what is not, and what should change.
Analyze recurring barriers, such as common reasons patients cannot be reached or questions that arise repeatedly, and develop recommendations that reduce the number of patients whose orders require intervention in the first place.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Process Improvement

Partner with Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Associate Clinical Oncology Specialists, and Patient Coordinators to set clear expectations, communicate promptly, and share accountability on every open case.
Partner with Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers to align program priorities, resolve regional barriers, and ensure teams understand their role in supporting patient orders.
Serve as the subject matter expert for ORP, providing guidance and consultation to field and operations partners and developing best practices, training, and standard work that can be adopted nationally.
Identify systemic process gaps and bring structured, data-backed recommendations to leadership, including changes to workflows, status definitions, tooling, and cross-team handoffs, with the patient experience as the guiding lens.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, life sciences, or a related field; or equivalent professional experience in a role requiring independent judgment, program ownership, and decision-making in a healthcare or clinical operations environment.
5 or more years of experience in healthcare operations, patient services, program or project management, or a comparable environment, with demonstrated ownership of a program, workflow, or initiative from assessment through execution.
Demonstrated ability to assess a complex operating landscape, identify root causes, and develop and present a data-supported recommendation, including resourcing and staffing needs, to senior leadership.
Proven ability to independently assess multi-variable situations and determine the appropriate course of action without direct supervision, particularly in patient-facing or clinically sensitive contexts.
Demonstrated ability to influence and drive accountability across cross-functional teams, including field, sales, and operations leaders, without direct authority.
Strong analytical capability, including building performance reporting, interpreting trends, and communicating findings clearly to leadership; advanced MS Excel or equivalent skills required.
Experience in a call center, patient outreach, or high-volume case management environment (inbound and outbound).
Proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and data tools; familiarity with skip tracing tools and LIMS is a strong plus.
Prior experience leading, coaching, or building a team is preferred. Background in patient coordination or another patient-facing healthcare role is strongly preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Technical

Program and project management expertise, including scoping, planning, prioritization, milestone tracking, and stakeholder management.
Specialized knowledge of healthcare operations, patient services workflows, and clinical coordination sufficient to evaluate case scenarios and develop resolution strategies without relying on standardized scripts.
Advanced proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and reporting tools, with the ability to design KPI dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into program performance and patient order outcomes.
Strong quantitative skills, including comfort working with large data sets to identify trends, build business cases, and model staffing and capacity needs.
Experience with skip tracing tools and multi-database research methods, and with process documentation and standard operating procedure development.

Behavioral

Exercises sound, independent judgment consistently, treating each case and each program decision as a situation requiring individualized analysis.
Builds before being asked: sees what a new program needs, takes ownership of the decision, and moves forward without waiting to be told something is off track.
Balances urgency and care: moves quickly because patients are waiting, and makes thoughtful decisions because the stakes are real.
Thinks like a program owner and acts like a teammate: comfortable working individual cases to learn the work, and equally comfortable stepping back to set strategy and advise leadership.
Earns credibility with cross-functional partners through expertise, clear communication, and follow-through, and uses it to drive action across teams they do not directly control.
Coaches and develops others, and is ready to build and lead a team as the program grows.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

This is a primarily remote position. Occasional on-site attendance may be required for planning sessions, leadership reviews, or business needs.
Duties are performed in a home office or professional office setting and require the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone, and read printed and digital material.
This role may require working outside standard business hours at times to address time-sensitive case situations or program needs.

Travel

Minimal travel required. Occasional travel (estimated less than 15%) may be required for national leadership meetings, regional business reviews, or planning sessions.

The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations.

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

jobs.title: Director, Talent Enablement Program Manager
jobs.description:
College Board - Global Strategy & Talent

Location: This is a remote role.

Candidates who live near CB offices may choose to work remotely or in a hybrid model (Tuesday/Wednesday in office). All employees are expected to travel occasionally for in-person business needs.

Role Type: This is a full-time position.

About The Team

At College Board, the Talent team is the engine behind our people who in turn power our mission to positively impact millions of students worldwide. We are a mission-driven group dedicated to enabling 2,000+ employees to do the most meaningful, high-impact work of their careers. As the world of work continues to evolve, the Talent team plays a critical role in helping College Board adapt with clarity, consistency, and purpose.

Guided by a clear philosophy, we design with the end user in mind, use data to solve real problems, innovate thoughtfully, and communicate directly and honestly. Our work is grounded in building high-performing teams, strengthening accountable leadership, and creating the conditions for every employee to thrive.

This role sits within the Talent Enablement Team, which designs and delivers the systems, tools, and learning experiences that empower employees to perform, grow, and lead. Talent Enablement defines what great performance looks like, builds the capabilities that enable it, and ensures employees have the clarity, feedback, and development needed to succeed, creating the infrastructure that drives consistency, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization.

About The Opportunity

The Director, Talent Enablement Program Manager is responsible for translating College Board’s talent strategy into accurate, well-run experiences and decision cycles for employees and managers. This role is accountable for the execution and continuous improvement of cycles such as engagement, rewards, and talent planning, ensuring they are delivered with rigor, clarity, and a strong user experience. Accountable for setting the design direction of these cycles within Talent strategy, the Director brings a clear point of view and recommends how they should evolve.

This role owns and executes the processes with high visibility and the sensitivity of comp-linked and talent decisions, works in close partnership with the Senior Director and Talent leadership, and requires strong judgment and discretion.

We are building towards a tech, data, and AI forward Talent function. As such, in partnership with Talent colleagues, GenAI partners, technology, and data teams, this role helps operationalize lighter-weight, AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual effort while improving quality.

Core Role Responsibilities

Cycle Design, Execution, and Continuous Improvement (50%)

Own the end-to-end design, delivery, and continuous improvement of a defined portfolio of College Board’s core talent cycles and decision processes such as role-leveling, goal-setting, calibration, bonuses, promotions, talent reviews, and employee engagement, in partnership with Talent Enablement peers to keep standards and the user experience consistent.
Partner with Finance, Compensation, Talent Tech, AI partners, and Data Analytics and others to identify improved systems, tools, workflows, and data that streamline processes and enable improved decisions.
Build and maintain internal program sources of truth and external-facing guidance and documentation for staff and support partners.
Owns detailed delivery plans and resolves cross-cycle dependencies and risks.
Gather and synthesize user feedback and operational insights after each cycle and translate feedback into concrete process, guidance, or workflow enhancements for future cycles.

Data- and AI-Enabled Workflow Delivery (25%)

Partner with GenAI, Technology, and Data partners to deliver AI-enabled improvements to talent processes.
Recommend and operationalize AI-enabled workflows in partnership with strategy and technical teams, translating design intent into real user experiences.
Runs Support pilots and releases that reduce manual effort and cognitive load while improving quality and data-driven decision making.
Ensure AI-enabled workflows are executed responsibly, aligned with enterprise governance, and clearly communicated to users.
Evaluate each workflow using execution insights, user feedback, and risks, and recommend whether to scale, change, or stop it.

Enablement, Communication & Stakeholder Partnership (25%)

Develop concise guidance, tools, training, and communications that enable leaders, employees, Talent Business Partners, and Specials to execute people processes well.
Lead cross-functional alignment across Talent, Finance, Compensation, Talent Business Partners, and other collaborators, and surface and resolve misalignment before it affects a cycle.
Advise the Senior Director directly on high-visibility rewards and talent decisions, exercising sound judgment around confidentiality.
Partner closely with Talent BPs, Specials, leaders, and managers to anticipate questions and reduce friction.
Bring a strong execution-informed point of view, contributing insights to strategy discussions.

About You

You are a leader who owns outcomes and turns strategy into reliable delivery. You execute complex, high-stakes cycles with rigor and discretion. You are comfortable working close to sensitive decisions and translating them into clear, well-run processes.

You Bring

6 - 8+ years of experience in program management, talent programs, engagement, performance, compensation, and rewards systems, with responsibility for executing complex, high-visibility, enterprise-wide cycles or initiatives.
A strong track record of operational excellence, including managing timelines, dependencies, risks, and stakeholder expectations across multiple teams.
Comfort partnering with Finance and Compensation on budget and allocation mechanics.
Comfort partnering with Technology and Data teams to deliver tools, workflows, or insights with high reliability and user trust.
Experience with supporting or operationalizing AI-enabled and technology-driven process improvements, with an emphasis on reducing friction to free people up to do uniquely human work.
Specific expertise with Claude, Workday, and Slack, including integration and automation between systems is strongly desired.
Strong communication and enablement skills, with the ability to translate complex processes into clear guidance and resources for diverse audiences.
Sound judgment and a collaborative mindset; able to bring a strong, execution-informed point of view while working within established strategic direction.
Experience with human-centered design and orientation, with the discipline to gather feedback, learn from delivery, and continuously improve systems over time.

All Roles At College Board Require

A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach To Compensation

The hiring range for this role is $80,000 - $135,000
Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

About College Board

College Board reaches more than 7 million students a year, helping them navigate the path from high school to college and career. We’re a mission-driven, not-for-profit membership organization dedicated to excellence in education. Founded 125 years ago, we are committed to clearing a path for all students to own their future. We pioneered programs like the SAT® and AP® to expand opportunities for students and help them develop the skills they need. Our BigFuture® program helps students plan for college, pay for college, and explore careers. Learn more at cb.org
.

Mission

Clearing a path for all students to own their future.

What Guides Us

At College Board, our work is guided by four Operating Principles, and we seek team members who not only align with these principles but actively live them out in their day-to-day work .

Prioritize and Simplify – We focus on what matters most, reduce complexity, and move quickly when needed.
Say and Receive – We give and receive feedback candidly and kindly, welcoming growth and healthy debate.
Go for Greatness – We pursue excellence using data, iteration, and bold thinking to raise the bar.
Lead as One College Board – We build a culture of trust, inclusion, and shared responsibility for long-term impact.

We Value and Provide Growth, Recognition, and Purpose

In addition to a competitive salary and benefits, we offer:

Annual bonuses and opportunities for merit-based raises and promotions
A mission-driven workplace where your impact matters
A team that invests in your development and success

✨Learn More ✨

Learn more about College Board’s Operating Principles, Our Remote-first Workplace Policy, Benefits, Recruiting Process and More.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Technical Program Manager - Network Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

Note: This position requires presence in our Bellevue or San Francisco office location 4 days per week; Lambda’s designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.

Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

Our vision is bold and is not an incremental exercise. We will continually re-evaluate and reinvent how we plan, build and operate our network, while running the existing network flawlessly for all customer workloads.

Lambda has 10x'd over the last three years, and the network engineering organization is scaling to match. We're looking for a Senior Staff Technical Program Manager to drive our top network infrastructure priorities: bringing network capacity online in new data centers, scaling the fabrics behind our largest GPU clusters, expanding external connectivity, and automating how we plan and deliver the network. These programs span network and software engineering disciplines as well as external partners. You'll own a high impact portfolio of programs critical to Lambda’s long term success, develop high confidence executable plans across teams, make tradeoffs visible to leadership, and keep execution on pace with our growth.

This role will report to the VP of Cloud and AI Networking, working alongside a highly capable and passionate team of engineers.

If you'd like to join a great team of customer obsessed engineers building the world's best AI cloud, come join us.

What You'll Do

Drive end-to-end delivery of Lambda's largest network infrastructure programs, from scoping and planning through execution and handoff to operations, so capacity is always ready ahead of customer demand. These programs are internal to networking specific but may span other organizations like product teams as we evolve.
Manage a portfolio of concurrent network programs, setting sequencing and priorities across them as business needs change
Help create simple but highly accurate tracking views/tools of top priorities internal to networking infrastructure organization.
Turn ambiguous goals into executable plans with clear scope, milestones, owners and dependencies, including long-lead hardware, vendor and construction timelines
Collaborate with engineering and product leaders to shape scalable, efficient solutions to the network problems that matter most to customers, such as cluster performance, connectivity and automating capacity delivery
Give senior leadership clear, regular reporting on progress, risks and decisions needed, with a recommendation attached to every escalation
Act as the main connection point between engineering and business teams, so that commitments made to customers and partners match what the network can deliver
Build durable processes for planning, release coordination and change management that hold up as the organization grows
Raise the program management bar across the network organization by mentoring other TPMs and sharing what works

You

Have 7+ years of technical program or technical product management experience, including leading large programs across multiple engineering teams
Have 10+ years of experience working directly with engineering teams
Have 5+ years of hands-on software development or network engineering experience, and can engage credibly on architecture, system design and technical tradeoffs
Have managed programs across cross-functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
Understand large-scale data center and cloud networking well enough to spot technical risk, challenge estimates and weigh tradeoffs with engineers
Have a track record of delivering complex infrastructure programs on schedule in fast-paced, high-growth environments
Are skilled at translating ambiguous business goals into clear priorities and executable plans
Use data and metrics to run programs and drive decisions
Show strong judgment about when to go deep technically, when to delegate, and when to escalate
Communicate clearly in writing and in person, and use written documents to frame decisions, align senior stakeholders and get approval on plans

Nice to Have

Experience in GPU cloud, HPC, or AI/ML infrastructure environments
Experience with high-performance cluster networking, such as InfiniBand or RoCE-based Ethernet fabrics
Experience with data center buildouts, network hardware supply chain, or long-lead capacity planning
Experience running programs that automate network planning, provisioning or operations
Prior experience at a high-growth infrastructure or cloud company

The annual salary range for this position has been set based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.

Founded in 2012, with 500+ employees, and growing fast
Our investors notably include TWG Global, US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Andra Capital, SGW, Andrej Karpathy, ARK Invest, Fincadia Advisors, G Squared, In-Q-Tel (IQT), KHK & Partners, NVIDIA, Pegatron, Supermicro, Wistron, Wiwynn, Gradient Ventures, Mercato Partners, SVB, 1517, and Crescent Cove
We have research papers accepted at top machine learning and graphics conferences, including NeurIPS, ICCV, SIGGRAPH, and TOG

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. Managing a database of projects and project milestones, complete with forecasting and completions across multiple facets of the network business
Leading cross-functional meetings to drive program productivity, completing and sharing meeting notes, and assigning action items
Collaborate, negotiate, communicate and execute across multiple cross-functional teams external and internal teams in order to achieve monthly and yearly goals

We’re looking for a scrappy, hands-on AI Product Technical Program Manager to join Figma Weave as the team’s first TPM. You’ll partner with Engineering, Product, and Design to turn ambiguous customer needs and new AI capabilities into reliable creative workflows. You’ll lead programs across the AI model lifecycle, usage economics, and products like the Weave API. You’ll get close to the architecture, help teams make informed technical tradeoffs, and stay accountable through launch and adoption. You’ll also build AI workflows and automation yourself to help the team move faster.

This full-time role can be based in our New York hub or remotely on the East Coast of the United States. You’ll join a team spread across the United States, Europe, and Tel Aviv, with occasional travel to work alongside Figma Weave partners in Tel Aviv.

What you’ll do at Figma Weave:

Lead model lifecycle management across image, video, editing, enhancement, audio/lip-sync, 3D, and vector models, using the existing evaluation process to drive new model integration, launch, updates, and deprecation
Make tradeoffs around quality, reliability, latency, cost, and capacity clear to the decision owners
Track model limitations, integration issues, and provider dependencies through fixes, rollout, and follow-up
Work with Engineering, Partnerships, and Finance on provider agreements, quotas, rate limits, and capacity commitments so Weave can support product growth and launch demand. Bring in Product, Legal, and Security to resolve dependencies
Manage AI costs, capacity, and unit economics across 10+ providers and 50+ models. Forecast usage and spend, plan provider capacity for launches, and work with engineers on fallback options
Build things that make work less work. Improve process design and build AI workflows and automation that help the team move faster. Use APIs, scripts, or data queries to improve program visibility, streamline processes, and remove recurring bottlenecks
Lead horizontal product programs that span Weave teams, such as the Weave API. Understand how API contracts, authentication, permissions, asynchronous execution, and usage limits affect delivery. Coordinate dependencies across Weave and Figma, work through technical blockers, and follow the program through testing, release, and adoption
Lead cross-functional technical readiness for Config and other major launches. Work with engineering leads on end-to-end workflow testing, provider capacity, monitoring, and rollback plans. Bring together Support, Legal, Marketing, and other launch partners, make risks and go/no-go decisions clear, and follow through on customer issues and incident action items after release

We’d love to hear from you if you have:

Scrappiness and adaptability: You get into the details and take practical steps to move work forward. You can investigate a problem, partner with your engineering counterparts on a solution, or build a quick prototype without waiting for a perfect plan. You adjust when priorities change and follow through on what you start
Third-party AI model integration: You’ve led programs that bring third-party AI models into a product and keep them working. You can use evaluation findings and usage data to drive decisions across Engineering, Product, and Partnerships, including tradeoffs around quality, reliability, latency, cost, capacity, and unit economics
AI-enabled process design and automation: Hands-on experience building lightweight processes by leveraging AI workflows, automation, or internal tools
Technical judgment and hands-on problem solving: You can follow a workflow from the user interface through backend services and external model APIs. You reason about latency, throughput, rate limits, retries, and failure modes with engineers. You’ve managed AI cost structures, including usage and spend, pricing negotiations, and capacity planning
AI product program delivery and ownership: You’ve led customer-facing technical programs with cross-functional partners, from an ambiguous need through launch and adoption. You judge success by whether the product works for customers and delivers the intended result

While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

You’ve been an early TPM or worked at a startup, where you helped engineering teams plan and ship without adding more process than they needed
You’ve worked with a broad set of model providers, including early-access programs or model migrations
AI research or applied AI program experience is preferred. You’ve partnered with researchers and engineers and used their findings to bring new capabilities into a product. Experience with generative image or video products, and how creative users judge output quality, is especially useful

jobs.description:
Job Description

WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?

RBC's AI-Driven Software Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) program is scaling across Technology & Operations through a franchise model. A central team owns the method, platform, measurement and playbook. Each L3 (Senior Executive) acts as a franchise, owning local execution, adoption and sustained ownership under a named AI-DLC Lead. With a target of 15,000 staff enabled by mid-FY27, the model depends on clear process and disciplined program management.

As Senior Program Manager, Change & Transformation, you will own delivery of the Franchise Model rollout, reporting to the Delivery & Exec Lead, Live Programs. You will be accountable for moving each L3 from kickoff to steady state on time: entry gates passed, 12-week adoption plan on track, and Central teams delivering what each L3 needs.

You will plan and sequence the rollout, coordinate L3 Leads and Central teams (Change & Learning, Platform, Benefits & Baseline), run the gate and waiver process with Technology ESG, and give decision-makers accurate, timely information. You must be comfortable in a high-visibility environment and able to hold direct conversations with Senior Director-level AI-DLC Leads about unmet gates.

WHAT WILL YOU DO?

Rollout Planning: Own the end-to-end L3 franchise rollout plan: sequencing, milestones, dependencies and calendar, from kickoff through steady state.
Entry Gates & Waivers: Drive each L3 through the five entry gates (roles staffed, readiness assessed, plan signed, platform ready, champion layer active) with L3 Leads and Technology ESG. Run the waiver process with a gap, closing date and owner, surface expiring waivers early, and allow no silent renewals.
Adoption & Readiness: Support each L3 through the 12-week adoption plan and readiness assessment, including white-glove or self-serve triage. Flag drift against handbook milestones and agree corrective actions with the Lead.
Central Team Coordination: Coordinate dependencies between L3s and Central teams (Live Programs, Change & Learning, Platform, Benefits & Baseline), and hold each team to its commitments. Resolve cross-L3 conflicts and capacity gaps, or take them to the right forum.
Forums & L3 Front Door: Run franchise forums, kickoffs, training and certification milestones, office hours and Demo Days. Route L3 questions to the right Central team, log them by topic, and track response times.
Tracking & Reporting: Maintain the franchise tracker as the single view of every L3 (gates, milestones, staffing, training, actions). Collect and check monthly funnel and RAG reports, and contribute content to Technology ESG and OC briefings with Lead Operations.
Escalation: Escalate off-track L3s or Central dependencies to the Delivery & Exec Lead and Technology ESG with context and a recommended path, and follow through to resolution. Work with the Program Manager to triage working-level issues.
Continuous Improvement: Capture feedback from L3 Leads, orchestrators and Change Champions, and analyze recurring questions, gate failures and blockers. Keep the handbook, templates and checklists current, and share lessons from early franchises.

WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED?

Must have:

Experience: 8+ years in program or delivery management within large-scale technology transformation, financial services, or enterprise change programs, ideally in a large regulated enterprise with formal governance structures
Multi-Stakeholder Rollout: Proven ability to run a rollout across many business units or teams, holding other leaders to commitments without direct authority.
Senior Stakeholder Management: Credibility to hold direct, candid conversations with Senior Directors and executive sponsors.
Process Discipline & Communication: Strong organization to track many concurrent workstreams, owners and deadlines accurately, with clear, concise written and verbal communication for senior audiences.
Tooling & Independence: Proficiency with JIRA, Confluence, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook, turning raw data into executive-facing views. Comfortable working independently in a vendor or staff augmentation capacity with minimal oversight.

Nice-to-have
:

Prior experience supporting AI, Agile, or SDLC transformation programs, or familiarity with AI-Native SDLC concepts.
Experience with a franchise, federated, hub-and-spoke or center-of-excellence rollout model.
Experience with change management, training rollout or adoption programs.
Familiarity with benefit measurement or baseline methodology.

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. to join our PMO team in Mexico City, Mexico, reporting to the Sr. Manager Business Operations. In this pivotal role, you will lead cross-functional company programs and COO initiatives through structured planning, data-driven execution, and clear business reporting.

Demonstrated commitment to inclusive collaboration, active listening, diverse perspectives, continuous learning, and shared success

Own the operating cadence and delivery rhythm for assigned programs, with clear plans, milestones, RAID management, decisions, and stakeholder communications

Contribute reusable PMO standards, templates, playbooks, and AI-enabled practices that can scale across Infoblox

Brief Posting Description

The P FT ADMIN - SAFETY Department of the P SAFETY Division at Hawaiian Electric Company has 1 Management vacancy available. This position may be filled on Oahu, Maui, or Hawaii Island. (Role: Professional)

Job Function

Plays key role in developing, promoting and maintaining a culture of safety at Hawaiian Electric Company. Serves as focal point for all safety program matters and is responsible for meeting all safety program related objectives. Develops, plans, organizes and implements Corporate Safety initiatives and programs in support of safety goals; manages scope and routinely audits programs and initiatives to assess program effectiveness. Ensures management of and coordination between internal and external parties in the development of safety programs and initiatives from program conceptualization to implementation to include planning, budgeting, design/development of written program, obtaining approval, implementation, delivering presentations & facilitating training, and monitoring/evaluating safety programs. Acts as the Corporate Safety Division’s liaison for safety programs developed by Safety Teams.

Essential Functions

Plans, organizes and manages all program activity associated with the planning, budgeting, design/development of written program, approval, implementation, presentation and training, and monitoring of safety programs. Provides program leadership, work direction and secures commitment from safety team members in meeting program milestones, goals and objectives. Works with team members to ensure access to resources and information; provides direction necessary to successfully perform in their roles. Develops strategies required to attain safety program goals. Regularly monitors programs to ensure early identification of potential problem areas. Actively engages to resolve problems to ensure attainment of program goals. Redirects to minimize constraints or actions which may delay schedules, effectiveness or add costs to safety programs.
Serves as the focal point for all safety program related matters. This requires addressing concerns; preparing, presenting, and conducting training for levels of internal and external groups; creating informational documents for wide distribution for all safety programs.
Establishes measurable matrix to routinely monitor safety programs for effectiveness of program objectives. Prepares and presents the progress and effectiveness of safety programs to all level of employees.

Coordinates with General Accounting and Budgets & Financial Analysis to review and approve procurement process of Safety Programs. Works on projects and initiatives as directed by Director of Safety Division.
Participates in Company emergency response activities as assigned, including any activities required to prepare for such emergency response.

Basic Qualifications

Knowledge Requirements

Extensive knowledge of project and program management principles normally acquired through college-level training, project/program management training and/or equivalent experience.
Working knowledge of OSHA, HIOSH, DOT, DOH, PUC, NIOSH rules, regulations and guidelines related to safety issues.
Program Management Professional (PMP) Certification from a nationally recognized organization such as the Program Management Institute (PMI) is highly desirable.
Working knowledge of general electrical utility, safety & health practices and industrial hygiene principals and techniques.
Working knowledge of personal computers and related software applications such as MS Project, Microsoft Word, Excel, Power Point, etc.

Skills Requirements

Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills.
Strong interpersonal skills to direct, influence, motivate and persuade groups or individuals.
Ability to handle difficult and/or sensitive issues while using tact, courtesy, and discretion.
Supervisory/leadership skills and abilities to work with a variety of individuals occasionally dealing with sensitive, difficult or confrontational issues and the ability to handle such issues with professionalism by using tact, courtesy, respect and discretion.
In-depth analytical, computational, organizational and time-management skills to handle various programs.
Ability to work collaboratively as a member of a team.
Ability to manage and develop/maintain strong positive relationships people at all levels within the company.
Ability to motivate/influence others in cross-functional teams over which this role has no direct authority.
Ability to remain flexible in a demanding work environment and adapt to rapidly changing priorities and strategic direction. Ability to operate as a self-starter and meet deadlines. Ability to conceptualize new ideas quickly.
Ability to conceptualize new ideas quickly.
Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license issued by the State of Hawaii or another U.S. state or territory. Must meet the standards for driving positions stated in the Company Driver Safety policy. These standards may be adjusted periodically to meet business and safety needs.

Experience Requirements

Extensive (5+ years) experience as a project or program manager preferably within safety and health issues related to the electric utility industry.
Several (3-5) years of industrial safety experience is desirable.
Several (3-5) years of experience in developing and implementing programs.
A few (1-2) years of experience in developing and conducting training.

jobs.title: Technical Project Manager
jobs.description:
The Red Hat Consulting team is looking for a Technical Project Manager to join us. In this role, you will manage complex projects from initiation through to delivery and completion.

You'll coordinate with cross-functional teams to complete distinct projects on time and within budget. As a Technical Project Manager, you’ll need to be organized and detail-oriented with substantial experience managing IT and software consulting projects, relying on traditional systems and software development methodologies.

What Will You Do

Lead and manage multiple customer-facing projects simultaneously to success
Manage project scope and customer expectations
Manage project risks, actions, issues, and dependencies (RAID)
Manage project budget and time frame
Build content for project activities like project kickoff, project status, and project closeout
Lead project meetings involving both customer and Red Hat’s consulting team members
Coordinate with territory services managers and the Resource Management Office (RMO) to manage project staffing requirements
Work with the service managers to ensure that financial forecast is up-to-date for their respective projects Support accounting activities as required, including obtaining copies of receipts for finance invoicing queries from customers
Develop basic knowledge of Red Hat’s technologies to guide successful project management, including Red Hat OpenStack Platform, Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform, Red Hat Ansible Automation, Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (JBoss EAP), Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and Red Hat Satellite Maintain professionalism when solving problems and resolving issues.

What Will You Bring

Knowledge of specific project management and software delivery methodologies like agile, scrum, Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe), and Project Management Institute (PMI)
Practical experience using various agile development tools like Trello, Rally, Atlassian Jira, or project management tools like Microsoft Project
5+ years of experience working as a project manager on IT or application development projects
Ability to affect, inspect, and adapt to culture
Demonstrated ability to motivate project team and individual contributors and to mediate conflicts.
Excellent customer-facing and internal communication skills
Great written and verbal communication skills
Solid organizational skills; attention to detail and ability to work on multiple tasks at the same time
Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience
Project management or scrum certifications are required
Experience with managing Government, and banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) customers is a plus

About Red Hat

Red Hat is the world’s leading provider of enterprise open source software solutions, using a community-powered approach to deliver high-performing Linux, cloud, container, and Kubernetes technologies. Spread across 40+ countries, our associates work flexibly across work environments, from in-office, to office-flex, to fully remote, depending on the requirements of their role. Red Hatters are encouraged to bring their best ideas, no matter their title or tenure. We're a leader in open source because of our open and inclusive environment. We hire creative, passionate people ready to contribute their ideas, help solve complex problems, and make an impact.

Inclusion at Red Hat

Red Hat’s culture is built on the open source principles of transparency, collaboration, and inclusion, where the best ideas can come from anywhere and anyone. When this is realized, it empowers people from different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences to come together to share ideas, challenge the status quo, and drive innovation. Our aspiration is that everyone experiences this culture with equal opportunity and access, and that all voices are not only heard but also celebrated. We hope you will join our celebration, and we welcome and encourage applicants from all the beautiful dimensions that compose our global village.

Equal Opportunity Policy (EEO)

Red Hat is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and an affirmative action employer. We review applications for employment without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, veteran status, genetic information, physical or mental disability, medical condition, marital status, or any other basis prohibited by law.
